He is taken to Laconia as Duarte's prisoner, Bobbie commands the ship, and Laconia rules humanity, having just attracted the notice of whatever killed the builders of the gates.

recaps.text: Previously: the crew of the Rocinante spent a decade at the center of every crisis in the solar system, from the alien protomolecule's destruction of the station Eros to the opening of the ring gates and the thousand-plus worlds behind them. The Belter revolutionary Marco Inaros threw asteroids at Earth and killed billions before his Free Navy was destroyed at the ring gate. Out of that settlement came the Transport Union, a Belter-led authority governing all traffic through the gates from Medina Station, which gave the Belt a permanent stake in the new worlds. One loose end was never resolved: a rogue Martian admiral, Winston Duarte, had taken roughly a third of the Martian navy and a sample of the protomolecule through the gates and disappeared into a system called Laconia. This book opens roughly thirty years later. Humanity has settled hundreds of worlds. Mars has been hollowed out by emigration, Earth is still recovering, and the union polices the gates. The Rocinante's crew are old: Holden and Naomi are preparing to retire and hand the ship to Bobbie Draper, with Alex still flying, Amos apparently unchanged, and Clarissa Mao aboard as a technician whose old implants are slowly killing her. Camina Drummer is president of the Transport Union. Nobody in Sol has heard anything from Laconia in thirty years.

The Rocinante is enforcing Transport Union rules at Freehold, a colony world that has refused to register its ships or acknowledge the union's authority over its gate. Holden settles it with a judgment designed to punish without killing anyone: Freehold loses its ships and its access to the gate for a generation, which its patriarch Payne Houston regards as a death sentence for the colony's independence and Holden regards as mercy. The crew's real preoccupation is retirement. Holden and Naomi mean to leave, Bobbie is to take the ship, and nobody is entirely comfortable saying so out loud. Meanwhile, thirty years of silence from the Laconia system is ending: Duarte's project there is finished, and the ships it produced are moving.

Laconia arrives. A single warship of a class nothing in human space can match enters the ring space, absorbs everything the Transport Union's defenses can throw at it without meaningful damage, and takes Medina Station. Admiral Trejo installs Santiago Singh as governor with orders to make the transition orderly. Singh, on his first independent command, believes that a firm, rational administration will convince Medina's population that the empire is an improvement, and treats compliance as something he can simply require. Holden and Naomi are on Medina when it falls. Drummer, at the head of a union that has just discovered its fleet is obsolete, has to decide what surrender is worth.

Laconia takes the rest of humanity. The Laconian flagship moves into Sol, where the combined fleets of Earth, Mars and the Transport Union meet it and are effectively destroyed without inflicting damage in return. Drummer publicly capitulates in order to keep the union intact and its people alive, a decision that costs her most of what she believed about herself. On Medina, Holden is arrested and held; Naomi avoids capture and disappears into the station's Belter infrastructure. Singh's administration begins to grind: rationing, registration, curfews, and the steady discovery that a population which cannot fight can still refuse. Saba starts assembling an underground out of union crews and Medina locals.

The occupation turns violent. Sabotage and an attack on Laconian personnel push Singh into reprisals he justifies as necessary, and each one recruits for the resistance. He orders a demonstration of force that kills civilians, alienates his own security staff, and destroys whatever consent his administration had. Trejo, away with the fleet, becomes increasingly concerned about the cost of what his governor is doing. Naomi, moving unseen through the station, works with Saba's cell; Holden, in custody, is a symbol both sides want to control. Amos, Alex, Bobbie and Clarissa keep the Rocinante hidden and prepare for the moment the station rises.

The underground commits to a rising timed against the Rocinante's escape. The plan requires the ship to be fought out of a defended station, the resistance to seize enough of Medina to cover it, and everyone involved to accept losses. Singh, isolated and convinced that only greater severity can restore order, prepares a response that would be catastrophic for the station's population, and his own officers begin weighing what their oaths actually require. Naomi, Saba and the crew make their final arrangements, knowing that whatever happens, none of them will be going back to the lives they were arguing about a few months earlier.

Medina rises and the Rocinante fights free, taking a Laconian destroyer with it. Singh is killed as the uprising unfolds, and Trejo assumes direct control and rescinds his worst policies. Clarissa Mao keeps the ship alive through the escape by driving her failing body past what it can survive, and dies. Holden surrenders himself to the Laconians in exchange for the Rocinante being released and Medina spared reprisals, and is taken to Laconia as Duarte's prisoner. Bobbie takes command of the ship with Alex and Amos aboard; Naomi stays behind the lines to organize the resistance. Drummer remains the public head of a Transport Union that now answers to Laconia, and quietly supports the underground. Humanity is under a single government for the first time. And the weapon Laconia used in the ring space has been noticed by something on the far side of the gates: ships have started vanishing in transit, and for one moment every mind in the ring space went dark at once.

characters.description: The widowed queen of Persia and mother of Xerxes. While the king and his army are away in Greece, she comes before the elders at Susa troubled by a dream and an ominous encounter between birds. Her questions draw out the contrast between Persian monarchy and the independent Greek cities, and her fear gives the distant war an immediate human cost.
characters.name: Atossa

characters.description: A council of elderly Persian nobles left in Susa while the younger men march with Xerxes. They begin in anxious admiration of the empire's power, question the messenger and the royal family, help call up Darius, and finally join Xerxes in mourning the disaster.
characters.name: Chorus of Persian Elders

characters.description: A survivor who reaches Susa from Greece with the first direct account of the expedition's defeat. He reports that Xerxes is alive but that much of the Persian leadership and fleet has been destroyed, turning the court's unease into public grief.
characters.name: Messenger

characters.description: The dead Persian king, husband of Atossa and father of Xerxes, summoned from the underworld by offerings and lamentation. He interprets Persia's defeat as the consequence of an overreaching campaign and warns that further suffering awaits the army still in Greece.
characters.name: Darius

characters.description: The Persian king and son of Atossa and Darius, who has led an immense invasion of Greece. He returns to Susa alive but stripped of his army and prestige, and his exchange of grief with the elders closes the tragedy.
characters.name: Xerxes

recaps.ending: Darius's ghost returns below after warning that the surviving Persian force will suffer another defeat at Plataea and that Persia should not again send an army into Greece. Atossa goes to fetch suitable clothing for her son. Xerxes then reaches Susa with only a remnant of his expedition, grieving for the commanders and soldiers lost in Greece. He and the chorus answer one another in a final lament over the fleet, the army, and the collapse of Persian confidence. Xerxes survives, but his attempt to extend Persian rule into Greece has ended in national bereavement and humiliation.
recaps.in_short: At the Persian court in Susa, elderly councillors and Queen Atossa wait anxiously for news of Xerxes's enormous expedition against Greece. A messenger arrives with word that the Persian fleet has been destroyed at Salamis after being drawn into confined waters, and that much of the army and its leadership has been lost during the retreat. Atossa and the elders summon the ghost of the former king Darius. He condemns the campaign's arrogance, warns of another Persian defeat at Plataea, and urges an end to invasions of Greece. Xerxes finally returns in torn clothing with only a fraction of his forces. The play closes with the defeated king and the chorus mourning the dead and the ruin of Persian power abroad.

recaps.text: In Susa, a chorus of elderly Persian nobles waits for news from the immense army that King Xerxes has led into Greece. Queen Atossa, disturbed by a symbolic dream and a troubling omen, asks the elders about Athens and the people her son is fighting. A messenger arrives and reports catastrophe: Xerxes lives, but the Persian fleet has been destroyed at Salamis after the Greeks lured it into waters where its numerical advantage could not be used. Many commanders are dead, and the army's retreat has brought further losses. Atossa and the elders make offerings and summon the ghost of her late husband, Darius. He rebukes the expedition's excesses, warns that the troops left in Greece face another defeat at Plataea, and tells Persia not to invade Greece again. After the ghost departs, Xerxes returns in disgrace with a shattered remnant of his force. King and chorus end the play in a shared lament for the dead and for the expedition's collapse.

characters.description: An itinerant former Army major who recognizes an indirect summons from his former superior, Tom O'Day, and accepts discreet transportation to an undisclosed destination.
characters.name: Jack Reacher

characters.description: A general and former superior of Jack Reacher who uses Rick Shoemaker to summon him.
characters.name: Tom O'Day

characters.description: A brigadier general who relays Tom O'Day's summons to Jack Reacher and arranges his discreet transportation to an undisclosed destination.
characters.name: Rick Shoemaker

characters.description: A young State Department officer based at Fort Bragg who receives Reacher at Pope Field. She introduces the known details of the extraordinary long-range shot in Paris and prepares him for the classified briefing.
characters.name: Casey Nice

characters.description: A missing former elite Army sniper whom Reacher investigated for murdering a Ranger sixteen years earlier. Recently released after a fifteen-year sentence, Kott is the American among four marksmen considered capable of the Paris shot.
characters.name: John Kott

characters.description: A senior CIA officer who joins the inquiry and explains the international consequences of a successful attack on several heads of state. Her prior work with Reacher's late brother Joe gives her a personal point of connection with him.
characters.name: Joan Scarangelo

characters.description: A former SAS sniper identified as one of four possible perpetrators of the Paris attack. His record includes an exceptional long-range kill, placing him among the few marksmen considered capable of the shot.
characters.name: William Carson

characters.description: A former Russian military sniper and one of the four candidates under international scrutiny after the Paris attack. Trained by a veteran of Stalingrad, he has the specialized skill required for an exceptionally difficult long-range shot.
characters.name: Fyodor Datsev

characters.description: A retired Israeli elite sniper considered among the four candidates capable of the Paris shot. Rosan is exceptionally skilled with a .50-caliber Barrett rifle.
characters.name: Rosan

characters.description: A former subordinate of Reacher who was killed after he sent her to arrest members of a criminal gang.
characters.name: Dominique Kohl

characters.description: A French ballistics investigator examining the Paris firing position. He recognizes that the first round was deliberately placed to damage the president's protective glass, then is killed by a distant rifle shot before he can carry the finding further.
characters.name: Yevgeniy Khenkin

characters.description: Jack Reacher's French mother, who died of lung cancer in 1990. As a child during World War II, she worked for the French Resistance by escorting Allied airmen through Paris.
characters.name: Josephine Moutier Reacher

characters.description: A British intelligence officer present with Reacher at the Paris firing site. When a sniper kills Yevgeniy Khenkin, Bennett immediately leaves the exposed balcony and avoids being recorded, demonstrating alertness to both physical danger and official scrutiny.
characters.name: Bennett

characters.description: An Albanian gang leader involved in London's drug, weapons, and trafficking trades. He is killed by a .50-caliber shot from long range, apparently as part of an arrangement between the marksmen and a local criminal organization.
characters.name: Karel Libor

characters.description: A figure identified among the Romford Boys leadership as Reacher's team investigates the east London organization suspected of supporting the wanted marksmen.
characters.name: White

characters.description: A figure identified among the Romford Boys leadership as Reacher's team investigates the criminal network believed to be protecting the wanted marksmen.
characters.name: Green

characters.description: A figure identified among the Romford Boys leadership as Reacher's team investigates the east London organization supporting the wanted marksmen.
characters.name: Miller

characters.description: A figure identified among the Romford Boys leadership as Reacher's team investigates the east London organization supporting the wanted marksmen.
characters.name: Thompson

characters.description: The seventy-seven-year-old boss of the Romford Boys, identified when intelligence details the east London gang's executive leadership.
characters.name: Charlie White

characters.description: The Romford Boys enforcer and a member of Charlie White's executive council. He is identified as the giant who recovered the gang's injured attacker.
characters.name: Joseph Green

characters.description: A member of Charlie White's executive council within the Romford Boys leadership.
characters.name: Tommy Miller

characters.description: A member of Charlie White's executive council within the Romford Boys leadership.
characters.name: Billy Thompson

characters.description: The apparent leader of a garage crew that confines Jack Reacher and Casey Nice after they arrive to buy weapons.
characters.name: Garage leader

characters.description: The leader of John Kott's security detail. Joseph Green arranges a delayed check-in with him, with instructions for the detail to leave the house if Green does not answer.
characters.name: Gary

characters.description: A woman heard inside the bedroom where John Kott is barricaded in Joseph Green's house. Her identity, condition, and relationship to Kott are not yet clear when Reacher first detects her presence during his search of the building.
characters.name: Unidentified woman

recaps.ending: Reacher, Nice, and Bennett escape the Romford Boys' custody. Reacher kills Joseph Green, and Green's unanswered check-in causes Kott's guards to leave the house. Reacher enters alone, disables Kott's rifle sight, and kills Kott while freeing an unidentified captive. Charlie White then threatens Reacher, but Nice approaches unseen and kills White. Reacher and Nice return to Pope Field, where Scarangelo explains that the apparent compromise of CIA communications was a controlled deception. Nice chooses to remain in intelligence. Reacher connects the Paris shot to armor that O'Day had personally seen withstand the relevant ammunition. He concludes that O'Day funded a one-shot demonstration that could not kill the protected target, hoping to create a crisis that would enhance his agency and either sacrifice Reacher or dispose of Kott. Reacher and Nice confront O'Day, preserve the information that could damage him, and avoid his aircraft. O'Day is subsequently reported dead from an accidental firearm discharge, but the actual circumstances of his death remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: After a long-range shot fails to kill the French president, General Tom O'Day recruits Jack Reacher to assess four possible marksmen. Evidence points to John Kott, a former Army sniper Reacher once sent to prison, and Reacher travels to London with intelligence officer Casey Nice. There they battle the Romford Boys, the gang sheltering Kott, while the supposed second shooter is eliminated from consideration. Reacher kills gang enforcer Joseph Green and then Kott, while Nice saves Reacher by killing gang boss Charlie White. Back in the United States, Reacher determines that the shot was never meant to penetrate the French armor. He accuses O'Day of financing a controlled demonstration to manufacture an intelligence crisis and improve his agency's standing. Reacher and Nice retain enough knowledge to threaten O'Day, who is later reported dead in an officially accidental shooting. Nice remains in intelligence, and the immediate assassination threat is over.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Reacher left the Army as a major and continued an itinerant life without a permanent home.

Eight days after a rifleman fires at the French president from extreme range, Jack Reacher notices a personal advertisement that directs him to Rick Shoemaker. The message is an indirect summons from General Tom O'Day, Reacher's former superior. At Fort Bragg, O'Day's team explains that the Paris shot may have been an audition for an attack on leaders at an international summit. Only four retired marksmen appear capable of it. The American candidate is John Kott, a former elite sniper whom Reacher helped convict of murdering a Ranger sixteen years earlier. Kott has completed his sentence and disappeared from his Arkansas home. Senior CIA officer Joan Scarangelo joins the inquiry, while Casey Nice is assigned as Reacher's field partner. Reacher and Nice travel to Arkansas, where Kott's neighbor provides little useful information. At the isolated property they discover a purpose-built firing platform and a target area exactly 1,400 yards away, matching the distance of the Paris attack. The matching range makes Kott the strongest American lead.

Kott's house contains Reacher's Army records and a life-size target bearing Reacher's likeness, showing that Kott has trained for a personal confrontation. Reacher also discovers that Casey Nice is a CIA officer temporarily presented as State Department staff. In Paris, ballistics investigator Yevgeniy Khenkin determines that the presidential shot was deliberately aimed to damage the protective glass. A distant sniper kills him before he can report the implication, and an apparent decoy helps divert the police toward Reacher. Reacher reconstructs a two-shooter operation: one marksman fired at the glass, while Kott waited to exploit the opening. He believes Kott later aimed at him but killed Khenkin when wind shifted the bullet. Ammunition evidence links that killing to fragments from Kott's Arkansas range. Meanwhile, Albanian gang leader Karel Libor is killed by another long-range shot in London. O'Day's team concludes that Kott and presumed British partner William Carson may be buying protection from the Romford Boys by eliminating a rival. Reacher and Nice are assigned to enter Britain without official protection and pursue the threat before the G8 meeting.

Security footage confirms that John Kott traveled from Paris toward London. Reacher and Nice arrive with encrypted communications and funds but no government weapons. They inspect Wallace Court, where the G8 leaders are scheduled to gather outdoors for photographs. Fyodor Datsev is located in Russian custody, leaving Kott and William Carson as the presumed active pair. Reacher maps possible sightlines toward the venue, but the investigation soon draws a response from the local support network. Two men posing as police attempt to confine Reacher and Nice in a panel van. Reacher overpowers them, and one dies from his injuries. Cash, forged identification, and a gang tattoo prove that the abductors are Romford Boys. Reacher and Nice leave the van where they can watch its recovery, turning the failed abduction into a probe of the organization. A very large enforcer retrieves the surviving man. British intelligence then identifies the gang's senior figures: elderly boss Charlie White, enforcer and executive member Joseph Green, and fellow council members Tommy Miller and Billy Thompson. The gang now knows that Reacher and Nice escaped, forcing them to abandon their lodging and relocate.

Reacher and Nice try to obtain pistols through a Serbian-connected criminal business, but the sellers imprison them while Joseph Green's men approach. They escape after a violent struggle in which Nice kills the garage leader in self-defense. Reacher finds concealed Glock pistols and ammunition, arms both of them, and calls the Romford Boys directly to demand the release of Kott and Carson. Nice struggles with having killed a man, but continues the mission. Bennett, the British intelligence officer from Paris, reappears and explains that his service has been monitoring their movements and communications. British authorities will observe and exploit the disruption caused by the Americans, but do not intend to provide open protection while British citizens are involved. Bennett moves Reacher and Nice to a Mayfair hotel and takes them to a covert observation post overlooking Joseph Green's unusually large, heavily guarded house. Surveillance shows that Green increased his personal security when the two marksmen first approached the Romford Boys, yet no visible transport or supply pattern reveals a separate hiding place. Reacher and Nice remain armed and operational, but neither Kott nor Carson has been sighted.

Reacher infers from the guard pattern and deliveries that Kott and Carson are hidden inside Joseph Green's house. At Wallace Court he studies the potential firing lines, then asks Bennett for classified information about the transparent armor used in Paris. He has begun to doubt that the G8 gathering is the true target. Reacher also tells Nice that he accepted the assignment partly because Rick Shoemaker once concealed an unlawful killing committed by Reacher during an earlier operation. Nice refuses to withdraw from the current danger. Because Green's house is hard to assault, Bennett proposes abducting Charlie White to provoke a succession struggle among the Romford Boys leaders. Reacher and Nice intercept White's car, overpower his escort, and take him to the former surveillance hut. Bennett arrives alone and explains that his team removed the monitoring equipment to prevent incriminating recordings. He also brings proof that William Carson died in Venezuela from an infected gunshot wound before the current climax. Carson therefore cannot be Kott's partner, leaving Kott as the sole active marksman. Reacher decides to use White as bait to draw Green away from the fortified house.

Joseph Green discovers the group at the surveillance hut, frees Charlie White, and captures Reacher, Nice, and Bennett. Reacher exploits the disorder around White's release, and the three prisoners overcome Green's guards. Green arranges a delayed check-in with Kott's security team, meaning they will abandon his house if he fails to answer. Reacher fights Green on the bowling green and kills him. The unanswered call sends Kott's four guards away. Bennett then produces the French armor report: the transparent shield can withstand the relevant armor-piercing ammunition, and Tom O'Day attended its trials. Reacher enters Green's oversized house alone. He locates Kott's loaded rifle and knocks its sight out of alignment, then finds Kott barricaded in a bedroom with a restrained woman. Reacher shoots Kott through a gap beside the door and frees the captive, who immediately injects herself with Kott's syringe and becomes incapacitated. While Reacher carries her out, White confronts him with a pistol. Nice approaches White unseen and shoots him, saving Reacher. With Green, Kott, and White dead, the immediate London operation ends. Reacher and Nice leave Bennett behind and board an RAF flight to the United States.

On the return flight, Nice decides to remain in intelligence rather than join the Army. At Pope Field, Joan Scarangelo reports that British authorities credit Reacher with enabling Kott's removal. She also explains that the CIA communications channel believed to be compromised carries deliberate false traffic, while a hidden replacement system uses weather-satellite data. Reacher remains troubled by the money behind Kott's operation. The armor report provides the answer: a real attempt to penetrate the shield would have required two shots in rapid succession, but Kott was assigned only one. Reacher concludes that the Paris attack was designed to fail safely and display the armor's effectiveness, creating an international intelligence crisis without killing the protected president. He accuses Tom O'Day of financing and directing the scheme to restore his standing, using Kott's hatred to endanger Reacher and planning for either man to eliminate the other. O'Day does not meaningfully answer the accusation. Reacher and Nice retain information capable of damaging him and avoid traveling on his aircraft. Reacher later learns that O'Day has died in what is officially called an accidental firearm discharge. The precise circumstances remain unknown, while the assassination threat and Kott's vendetta are ended.
